To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the autoimmune sialitis of the non‐obese diabetes (NOD) mouse is characterized by a restricted use of T cell receptor variable β (TCR‐Vβ) elements, and the autoimmune response in NOD mice is driven by common T cell clones.

the autoimmune sialoadenitis of non‐OBese diabetic (Nod) mice has a restricted usage of t cell receptor (tcr) vβ elements in the infiltrating t cells, which is different from that observed in the insulitis of NOD.
T cell‐mediation autoimmune sialadenitits in the NOD mice is driven by restricted usage of T cell receptor variable (TCR V) β elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the autoimmune sialoadenitis of NOD mouse.
the TCR Vβ usage of the autoimmune sialoadenitis in NOD mice.
the analysis of T cell receptor usage in the autoimmune lesion of the salivary gland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cell‐mediatd autoimmune sialadenits of NOD mice is characterized by a restricted usage of Vβ elements.
in autoimmune sialadenitits of NOD mice there may be a limited T cell receptor repertoire in the early stage.
there are some differences and similarities between the autoimmune insulitis and sialadenitis in the NOD mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Vβ8+ and Vβ6+ T cell subsets may play a major role in the development of autoimmune salivary gland disease.
the autoimmune sialoadenitis of NOD mouse is a T‐cell mediated disease.
the Vβ8 gene segment was more often used in the salivard glands, and the Vβ8.2 gene segment was the most frequently used gene segment in the salivad glands of NOD mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the autoimmune sialdenitis of NOD mouse is a TCR Vβ‐restricted disease.
T cell clonal selection and expansion is an important feature of organ‐specific autoimmune disease.
there may be a restriction on TCR Vβ usage in autoimmune sialadenitits of NOD mice.
